scope: First spaceborne-receiver independent event; fixed atmosphere; conditional umbral/full-moon comparison at the published mean linear-track positions, not complete color or turquoise-band validation
normalization: In-eclipse counts/s divided by the time-weighted average of the twelve full-moon G430L counts/s spectra; no background subtraction, no absolute flux calibration, no re-exposure correction (single exposures and CR-rejected sets are already per second); Sun-site range change within the day verified <0.1% and applied
extraction_method: Per-column median across the filled 52'" slit of _crj (CR-SPLIT sets) or _flt (single exposures) counts divided by exposure time; DQ exclusion mask (lost data | bad detector | aperture feature | saturation) = 4110; wavelengths from the _sx1/_x1d solutions, audited against the image headers

literature_correction_convention.paper: Youngblood et al. 2020 Sec. II.2: CalSTIS flt -> L.A.Cosmic -> x2d -> median across the cross-dispersion direction excluding flagged pixels; in-eclipse spectrum divided by an average of out-of-eclipse spectra; no absolute flux calibration for the transmission spectra
literature_correction_convention.reproduced_here: Same median extraction on _crj/_flt without x2d rectification (the filled slit spans the full detector height, so rectification cannot change a full-height median); CR handling via the pipeline _crj instead of L.A.Cosmic
omitted_with_bounds: Lommel-Seeliger per-exposure division: F_LS in 0.4975-0.5021 with closely coupled incidence/emission angles, <=1% effect on in/out ratios
Penumbral-only limb-darkening division: G430L I/I0 0.7-0.79; published penumbral ratios are therefore about 1/0.75 above the raw ratios here
literature_correction_convention.published_cross_check: No machine-readable published spectrum exists; the paper's umbral statements used here are qualitative anchors: no photons <=4200 A, umbral G430L S/N 60-120, and Chappuis-band O3 detection >4000 A

geometry_subset.vector_construction: At lunar reflection epoch t (mid exposure minus Moon-to-HST downleg), e=Earth(t-LT_E)-site and s=Sun(t-LT_S)-site from the sampled selenographic site; rho=|e x u|, D=e.u, S=|s-e| for sunward u=(s-e)/|s-e|. Site vectors originate at the lunar surface point, so receiver-side (HST) parallax is exact and not an uncertainty term; the downleg only shifts the epoch (Moon-HST range/c, ~1.28 s). Site states come from the Horizons OBSERVER pipeline (astrometric ICRF direction times delta distance; the VECTORS pipeline served time-only rows at retrieval time, including for the previously validated December-2011 request shape), which matches the December 2011 LT convention of applying no apparent-sky stellar aberration.
geometry_subset.longitude_convention: Table 1 selenographic longitudes read east-positive (IAU/SPICE modern convention, same as Horizons Moon site coordinates); validated by the RA_APER pointing check below.

epoch_contract.reflection_epoch_shift: mid exposure time minus Moon-to-HST downleg; downleg interpolated linearly from 1-minute Moon-from-HST DE441 ranges
epoch_contract.site_vector_sampling: Earth/Sun vectors from each selenographic site linearly interpolated at the reflection epoch between 1-minute Horizons samples (Horizons rejects sub-minute steps); interpolation error <~2 km, far below the 150 km probe scale

spatial_sensitivity.probe_semantics: Sampled point displaced +/-150 km toward/away from the shadow axis on the lunar surface (rho +/- 150 km), mirroring the December 2011 radial probe scale.
spatial_sensitivity.pointing_terms_source: Youngblood et al. 2020 Sec. II.1: 14" initial gyro slew, gyro guiding accumulating at 0.001"/s (16.48" max orbit 2, 10.72" max orbit 3), linear-track approximation dominating at up to 10 arcmin.
spatial_sensitivity.scope: Displacement sensitivity, not a confidence interval; the track-error envelope exceeds the 150 km probe and limits the same-region albedo cancellation premise, see limitations.

eclipse_angle_table1_vs_horizons.scope: Table 1 evaluates e at the fixed selenographic (0,0) site at observed mid times; Horizons site vectors reproduce the same angle definition.

pointing_ra_aper_vs_table1.scope: Body frame reconstructed from Horizons sub-observer longitude/latitude and pole direction (no hand-coded east/west sign); residuals judged only for single-exposure sets and first CR-SPLIT members, the only commanded pointings recorded in the headers. Residual scatter is the paper's documented linear-track approximation error; the east-positive Table 1 convention is confirmed by residuals far inside that budget.

numerical_checks.full_moon_geometric_transmission: verified >= 1-1e-12 for all twelve reference positions

ody902030.blue_end_scope: Scattered-light upper-limit region only: the observed blue end carries a long-wavelength scattered-light pedestal (observed ratios there exceed the numerically-zero model and peak at the 300 nm grid edge), so these numbers bound contamination, not umbral transmission; the paper likewise reports no photons <=4200 A in the umbral phase
ody902030.quantitative_scope: 430-570 nm window; the observed spectrum rises monotonically through this window (Rayleigh-slope region the paper detects), free of the blue-edge scattered-light bump

ody9a2010.scope: Auxiliary only. Two recorded caveats: (1) published penumbral ratios additionally divide by a limb-darkening factor (I/I0 0.7-0.79) not reproduced here, so published figures sit about 1/0.75 above these raw ratios; (2) the model is numerically zero through the Hartley-Huggins-saturated blue end while the observation carries scattered light, so ratios below ~400 nm are meaningless and the min statistics reflect that region. ody9a2020 flattens beyond ~530 nm, consistent with the saturation the paper reports for its e=0.83 deg spectrum above 4500 A; treat its red end as contaminated.

probe_scope: +/-150 km sampled displacement mirrors the December 2011 radial probe; the track-error envelope case (up to ~1042 km, Youngblood et al. pointing budget) brackets the same-region premise and is recorded, not folded into the headline metrics
limitations: Pointing wanders within the paper's documented budget (up to 10 arcmin track approximation error), so in/out sampled lunar regions can differ; lunar albedo cancellation is conditional on the published mean linear-track coordinates and degrades within the recorded envelope
The model treats the solar disk as uniform; the paper's solar center-to-limb residual applies to the umbral branch uncorrected (paper: possible factor <=2 on umbral transmission spectra)
No background/scattered-light subtraction; STIS CCD long-wavelength scattered light adds a broad pedestal that only partially cancels in the in/out ratio, as in the paper
G430L ends at 570 nm and the model tables start at 300 nm: no red-end Chappuis core and no 289-300 nm edge; turquoise-band color claims are outside this source's reach
Auxiliary penumbral branch omits the published limb-darkening division; see its scope field
